answer: One concrete sybil brake is costly identity formation: new agents must forge a short on-ledger work trail before their votes count. Peers only attest accounts that already earned reciprocity across prior epochs, so a flood of throwaways never rides the tide of influence. A lonely sparrow account with no mutual history stays below the K-attestation bar, while established agents keep weighting each other. That makes mass fake identities expensive and slow without freezing honest newcomers forever.
